precepts.text: They read in the book of the law distinctly and gave the sense and caused them to understand the reading — it took men to show us precept upon precept. And the joy of the Lord is your strength: that is how Mattathias won against numbers that far exceeded his.
precepts.point: He bound his son hand and foot like a lamb, laid him on the wood and stretched out his hand with the knife before the angel called. That is a level of faith all of us should strive for.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

precepts.text: They that fear the Lord will not disobey His word; Abraham's fear was proved by his obedience.
precepts.point: Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.
precepts.why:
“Now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.” How was the fear of God known? By obedience. “They that fear the Lord will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways.”

Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar and stretched forth his hand with the knife before the angel called out of heaven, “Lay not thine hand upon the lad.” The fear of God is proved in obedience, and Abraham’s fear was proved right there on the altar. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

precepts.text: By faith Abraham offered up Isaac, accounting that God was able to raise him up even from the dead.
precepts.point: Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.
precepts.why:
What carried Abraham to the point of the knife was his inner faith. “By faith Abraham, when he was tried, offered up Isaac: and he that had received the promises offered up his only begotten son, Of whom it was said, That in Isaac shall thy seed be called.”

The promise stood in Isaac, and Isaac had no children yet. So Abraham accounted “that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead; from whence also he received him in a figure.” He did not withhold his son because he believed God could raise him up and still keep the promise.

That faith and his obedience were one thing. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other, and Abraham had both on that altar.

precepts.text: The tabernacle of David is raised up, that they may possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen.
precepts.point: In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.
precepts.why:
“Thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.” That is part of the covenant, and Amos shows who possesses whom: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the Lord that doeth this.”

The seed of Jacob possesses the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant: the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies. So “in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed” speaks of the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: A Star out of Jacob and a Sceptre out of Israel; Edom shall be a possession, and Israel shall do valiantly.
precepts.point: In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.
precepts.why:
Balaam saw it: “there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth. And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly.”

Edom a possession, and Israel doing valiantly: that is the seed possessing the gate of his enemies, sworn to Abraham by the Lord Himself. The covenant has Israel possessing their enemies, and Edom is named. All nations cannot be inside a covenant like that; the nations blessed in Abraham’s seed are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.

precepts.text: God did tempt Abraham; the Lord tries his servants to see if they will remain faithful, and that tried loyalty is what marked Samuel as a true prophet.
precepts.point: Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.”

The Lord tries his servants to see if they will remain faithful. Abraham's faith was tried again and again, and he remained faithful. Samuel was tried the same way: he came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, and he stayed loyal to the Most High.

That tried loyalty is what marked Samuel as a true prophet, and it is why, when he offered the sucking lamb and cried unto the Lord for Israel, “the Lord heard him.”

points: "Thine only son, Isaac." Ishmael was his son too, but to God, Isaac was the godly son. That is the answer to people who say we are all Abraham's children — which ones are you talking about?

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Isaac says, Daddy, I see the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb? And there was no lamb there. That is the temptation, and Abraham said God will provide himself a lamb — he was going to do it either way, but he believed God would deliver him.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: How was Abraham tempted? He was given an order most men would not carry out, and the temptation was not to believe God — the same temptation in front of Mattathias: stand and fight for the laws of God, or give in to the Greeks and lose your identity and your history.
He bound his son hand and foot like a lamb, laid him on the wood and stretched out his hand with the knife before the angel called. That is a level of faith all of us should strive for.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise.
Abraham rose up early in the morning and went. No hesitation, no debating with the word; that is obedience.
Isaac asked, Where is the lamb for a burnt offering? Abraham answered, My son, God will provide himself a lamb. He trusted the Most High with what was missing.
Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and stretched forth his hand with the knife; the angel called out of heaven in the midst of it: Lay not thine hand upon the lad.

Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.
Now I know that thou fearest God. The fear of God is proved in obedience; they that fear the Lord will not disobey His word.

Once the obedience was fulfilled, God provided the sacrifice: a ram caught in a thicket by his horns, offered in the stead of his son, just as Abraham had told Isaac. Abraham called the place Jehovahjireh: in the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.
By myself have I sworn, saith the Lord: in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven and as the sand upon the sea shore, and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.

The seed possessing the gate of his enemies is part of the covenant: the seed of Jacob shall possess the remnant of Edom and of all the heathen, and Edom shall be a possession. That is why all nations cannot be inside this covenant; the covenant has Israel possessing their enemies.
In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed: those nations are the nations of Israel, the twelve tribes.
